1.steps:
1.Click the add button to add a NM policy
2.On the pop up window type in following characters in the name field; testPolicy Test12 !@$ 123456
3.Choose a probe target and then click ok.
1.title: GUI functionality - Format check for Name field.
1.description: This case is to verify the format of the name field
1.result: The first three characters can be accepted as the Name, while numbers should not be allowed, an error will come up Error: Network Object names cannot be numbers.

10.title: GUI functionality- Edit an Object that is selected as the gateway or probe target.
10.description: This case is to verify that an object that is in use as the gateway or probe target can be edited.
10.result: The object should be updated accordingly on the Network monitor policies table.

11.title: Negative test- Change the AO that is in use by a policy to a wrong type.
11.description: This case is to verify that firewall will report error when change the AO that is in use by a NM policy to a wrong type which is not accepted by the field.
11.result: Step 5 and 6 should not be allowed. No crash happens and firewall will report error that the AO type is wrong.

14.title: GUI functionality - Boundary check for port option.
14.description: This case is to check the boundary of port option.

15.steps:
1.Open the add NM policy window on Network Monitor Policies page;
2.Enter a policy name, and select a probe target;
3.Enter a value other than integer for following probe parameters and then click ok:
a)Port number
b)Probe interval
c)Reply timeout
d)Failure threshold
e)Success threshold
4.Re-enter an integer for these parameters and click OK.
15.title: GUI functionality - Format check for probe parameters.
15.description: This case is to verify the format of the probe parameters should be Integer.
15.result: For values other than integer, firewall will report error Data is incorrectly formatted.

16.steps:

Enter a policy name, and select a probe target;
Enter following value for probe intervals and then click the ok button.
0
9999
60
1
3600
16.title: GUI functionality - boundary check for probe intervals.
16.description: This case is to verify the boundary value of probe intervals.

17.steps:
Open the add NM policy window on Network Monitor Policies page;
Enter a policy name, and select a probe target;
Leave default value 5 as the probe interval, then enter following value for reply timeout:
0
10
3
1

Change probe interval value to 100, then enter following value for reply timeout:
60,
80.
17.title: GUI functionality-boundary check for reply timeout.
17.description: This case is to verify the boundary value for reply timeout.

18.steps:
Open the add NM policy window on Network Monitor Policies page;
Enter a policy name, and select a probe target;
Enter following value for missed intervals and then click the ok button.
0
200
1
100
18.title: GUI functionality-boundary test for failure threshold.
18.description: This case is to verify the boundary value of failure threshold.
18.result:
For value 0, firewall will report: Please specify a threshold for missed intervals.
For value200, firewall will report: Error: Missed Probes: Data out of bounds (min = 1, max = 100).
Value1 and 100 will be accepted by firewall.

Enter a policy name, and select a probe target;
Enter following value for missed intervals and then click the ok button.
0
200
1
100
19.title: GUI functionality-boundary test for success threshold.
19.description: This case is to verify the boundary value of success threshold.

For value200, firewall will report: Error: Successful Probes: Data out of bounds (min = 1, max = 100).

2.steps:
1.Try to add a NM policy with the name field empty;
2.Click the ok button.
2.title: GUI functionality - Empty Name is not allowed.
2.description: This case is to verify error handle when name field is empty.
2.result: The policy should not be added; an error message should come up Please enter a policy name.

20.title: GUI functionality- All must respond option can be checked/unchecked.
20.description: This case is to verify the option All must respond can be checked.
20.result: All must respond can be selected and its value will set to 1 in the TSR once selected.

21.title: GUI functionality - comment field.
21.description: This case is to verify the comment field.
21.result: Policy added successfully and comments can be displayed correctly when put mouse over the comments icon.

25.steps:
1.Add several NM policies;
2.Click the delete all button.
25.title: Button functionality- Delete all NM policies.
25.description: This case is to verify delete all button works well to delete all the policies.
25.result: All custom policies should be deleted successfully.

26.title: Negative test - Delete a policy that is in use by a route.
26.description: This case is to verify a policy that is in use by a route can not be deleted.
26.result:
The policy can not be deleted, firewall will report following errors:
Object is in use by a Route Policy.
Cannot delete this Network Monitor entry.

27.title: Button functionality- Clear statistics.
27.description: This case is to verify clear statistics button works well.
27.result: Statistics 1 to 4 of all the policies should be cleared and set to zero.

3.title: GUI functionality  Policy name must be unique.
3.description: This case is to verify each NM policy must be given a unique name.
3.result: The second policy should not be added and firewall should report error like policy already exists.

31.title: Auto-added policies can not be deleted by delete button or delete all button.
31.description: This case is to verify delete or delete all button only take effects for custom policies.
31.result: All the NAT probe policies should not be deleted.

32.title: Auto-added policies can be edited through Advanced settings of NAT policy.
32.description: This case is to verify auto-added policies can be edited through advanced NAT.
32.result:
NAT probe polices can be edited successfully through advanced NAT.
The pseudo-LED turns yellow and all statistics of this policy has been cleared at first.

33.title: Auto-added policies can be deleted through Advanced settings of NAT policy.
33.description: This case is to verify NAT probe policies will be deleted if enable probing is disabled on advanced NAT.
33.result: The auto-added NAT probe policy is deleted on the NM policies table.

4.steps:
1.Click the add button on Network Monitor Policies page;
2.In the Name field, try to enter more than 32 characters.
4.title: GUI functionality - Max length of the Name field.
4.description: This case is to verify max 32 characters can be entered in the Name field.
4.result: Only 32 characters in maximum can be entered and this name can be displayed correctly in Name column.

42.title: Functional test for probe target of Host type.
42.description: This case is to verify Host object can be probed successfully.
42.result:
Policy status should be up after three successful intervals, and will change to down after three missed intervals when egress interface disconnected.
Mouse over of the policy status should show the probe statistics and the status of the host target: up or down.

43.title: Functional test for probe target of Range type.
43.description: This case is to verify Range object can be probed successfully.
43.result:
Policy status should be up if one of the host within the range is up. And will change to down when all the hosts status are down.
Mouse over of the policy status should show the probe statistics and the status of all the host targets within the RangeAO.

44.title: Functional test for probe target of FQDN type.
44.description: This case is to verify FQDN object can be probed successfully.
44.result: All resolved ip address of the FQDN can be probed successfully.

45.title: Functional test for probe target of Group type.
45.description: This case is to verify Group object(host, range, or FQDN objects only) can be probed successfully.
45.result:
Policy status should be up if one of the members in the group is up.
Mouse over of the policy status should show the probe statistics and the status of all the ip addresses in the group including host, range and FQDN.

47.title: Functional test for option All hosts must respond.
47.description: This case is to verify the function of All hosts must respond.
47.result: Policy status will be set to down as long as theres one host status is down. Only when all the probe hosts are up, policy status changes to UP.

57.title: Create a new monitor policy from the add route dialog.
57.description: This case is to verify monitor policy can be added through the add route dialog.
57.result: The NM policy can be added successfully and selected as the probe policy of the route.

58.title: Functional test for option Disable route when probe succeeds.
58.description: This case is to verify the static route will be disabled when the probe policy is up.
58.result: The static route should be grayed-out when probe succeeds and active when the probe fails.

59.title: Functional test for option Probe default state is UP.
59.description: This case is to verify the static route with an unknown status policy should be active when option Probe default state is up is selected.
59.result: The static route should be active when policy is in unknown status if the option Probe default state is up is selected.

6.steps:
1.Open the add NM policy window on Network Monitor Policies page;
2.Enter a policy name, leave other fields as default, then click the ok button.
6.title: GUI functionality - Empty probe target is not allowed.
6.description: This case is to verify a probe target must be selected in a NM policy.
6.result: Policy should not be added with an error message Please select a probe target.

72.steps: 1.Add several NM policies; 2.Add some static route with probe policies selected; 3.On CLI, type the command: show tsr network,verify all the NM policies are displayed; 4.Type the command:show route,verify the pepbr can be displayed correctly. Note: in step3, command is "show tech-support-report network-monitor" in 7.1.0, otherwise, it should be "show network-monitor policies". "show tsr network" can't be work.
72.title: CLI support for NM policies configuration.
72.description: This case is to verify PEPBR info can be viewed or configured on CLI. Currently, it hasn't been exploited to configure NM policy or PEPBR on CLI but these info can be viewed on CLI.
72.result: NM policies and PEPBR info can be viewed from CLI.

8.title: GUI functionality  Gateway and Interface can be specified for explicit route probe.
8.description: This case is to verify Interface option should be disabled when select Ping or TCP probe.
8.result: Policy with specified gateway and Egress interface can be added successfully.

9.title: GUI functionality  Delete an Object that is selected as the Gateway or probe target.
9.description: This case is to verify object can not be deleted when its selected as the Gateway or probe target.
9.result: Operation should be denied with an error message: Error: Object is in use by a Network Monitor policy.
